analysis.investment_thesis: A recently-listed micro-cap with a suspiciously sharp pre-IPO earnings jump (net profit 1→3→14 Cr over 2023-2025), debt-to-equity of 1.16, and effectively zero cash — this fails nearly every quantitative filter I require. The 73.8% ROE is an arithmetic artefact of a tiny 29 Cr equity base, not evidence of durable earning power.
key_strengths: P/E of 11.1 is within my <15 threshold on trailing earnings
Revenue CAGR of 20.5% (2021→2025) shows genuine top-line traction
OCF turned positive from 2023 and reached 15 Cr in 2025, matching reported profit
key_risks: Debt/equity of 1.16 is 2x my ceiling; borrowings 33 Cr vs cash ~0
No multi-year earnings record — profit was near-zero through 2022 and only meaningful in 2025
Pre-IPO earnings spike (3 Cr→14 Cr in one year) is classic IPO window-dressing pattern
red_flags: Zero cash on balance sheet in 2023, 2024, 2025 — severe liquidity fragility
Recent listing (BSE code 544671) — seller/underwriter knows more than buyer
Earnings quadrupled in the year immediately preceding/following listing
Promoter holding 73% — low public float, thin liquidity
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Graham lens, this company fails the foundational test: a stable, demonstrated earning power over 5-10 years. Net profits of 0, 0, 1, 3, and 14 Cr do not constitute an earnings record — they constitute a hockey stick coinciding with a listing event. The headline ROE of 73.8% is produced by dividing 14 Cr of profit by a sliver-thin 29 Cr equity base, much of which is recently retained. Leverage is the mirror image of that thin equity: 33 Cr of borrowings against ~zero cash and 3 Cr of annual interest cost leaves a fragile interest-coverage picture that could unravel in any cyclical downturn in Indian construction capex.

The business itself — HDD and foundation drilling rigs — is legitimate and cyclically tied to Indian infrastructure build-out, but that is a story for a growth investor, not for me. I need a margin of safety measured in assets and proven earnings. With P/B implied near 3.4x (price 99.8 vs book ~29 Cr on a small share count) and only one year of material profit, there is no such margin. I would require either a 50%+ drawdown or three more consecutive years of stable 10+ Cr earnings with debt halved before reconsidering. Avoid.
